newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa wants more cash in '97 for Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Dasa wants more cash in '97 for Eurofighter.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), the German partner in the Eurofighter project, said on Thursday that not enough cash had been pencilled into Bonn's 1997 budget to pay for startup production of the combat jet.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's draft budget, which was being reviewed by a parliamentary committee on Thursday, sets aside 100 million marks for Eurofighter next year.
"This sum is clearly not enough for serial production. We need at least 392 million marks," Dasa spokesman Christian Poppe told Reuters.
Although it has earmarked some funding for Eurofighter, the cash-strapped German government this week put off until January a decision on placing a firm order for its 180 Eurofighters.
Dasa has a 30 percent stake in the Eurofighter consortium and its main task will be to build the fuselages of the production run of 620 aircraft.
British Aerospace (Bae) owns 37.5 percent of the project, Italy's Alenia 19.5 percent and Spain's Casa 13 percent.
The first aircraft are due for delivery in 2001 -- a target which BAe said could still be met if Germany follows Britain and Spain in committing to buy its Eurofighters in early 1997.

"If production investment is available in the first quarter of next year then we can meet the deliveries due to the Royal Air Force on time in 2001, for squadron service in 2002," a BAe spokesman told Reuters in London.

Germany's defence ministry declined to comment on the state of the negotiations -- but Dasa's Poppe said talks were continuing to try and "bridge the gap" on payment terms. He gave no forecast of when they might reach a conclusion.

Poppe also denied a newspaper report this week which said that Juergen Schrempp, head of Dasa parent Daimler-Benz, had offered to cut the overall cost of Eurofighter to Germany to 23.3 billion marks from 26 billion.
"It stays at 26 billion marks," he said.
